name: Grok
tagline: xAI's chat assistant, sold through paid xAI and X subscription tiers, with access to real-time X data.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. xAI has shuffled tier names and prices repeatedly and access is bundled with X subscriptions, so no number is asserted here.

verdictSummary: You are not one-shotting a frontier language model. The chat interface around it is genuinely trivial, a weekend intern could ship a better one, but the interface is not what you are paying for: you are paying for a multi-billion-dollar training run and the GPUs that serve it. The one differentiator that is not just raw model quality, live access to the X firehose, is a licensing relationship you cannot replicate at any price. What you can build in a session is a good local chat client that talks to whatever model API keys you already have, or to a local model on your own machine, which is a real product but a different one. Call it a consolation build, not a replacement.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted streaming chat UI with saved conversations, system prompts and swappable model backends, pointed at an API key you supply or a local model.
requirements: An API key for some model provider, or a machine that can run a local model via Ollama
Acceptance that the model quality is whatever you paid for elsewhere
whatYouLose: The actual model. Nothing you build changes which weights answer you.
Real-time X data and the licensing that makes it legal at scale.
Mobile and voice apps, image understanding, image generation, all the surrounding surface area.
Someone else eating the inference cost and latency engineering.
Anything resembling a support path when it starts confidently lying to you.
moatNotes: Frontier models are the clearest capital moat in software right now: the cost floor is a datacenter, not a developer.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the product is the model, and models are not code you can write, they are capital you can rent. A subscription buys frontier-tier inference with no cold start, no GPU bill, no quantization tradeoffs, plus mobile apps and a live data feed you cannot license as an individual. The chat wrapper is a rounding error in the value. People who self-host still end up paying someone for the weights or the tokens; the only real question is whether you want one bill or four.
notes: The chat window is a Saturday afternoon; the thing answering you is a datacenter. The moat is the training run, the serving fleet, and a data licensing deal with X that no individual can buy.
prompt:
Build a local, self-hosted chat client for large language models. Single user, runs on my machine, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Bun + Hono for the server, TypeScript.
- SQLite via bun:sqlite for storage. One file, chat.db, created on first run.
- Frontend: one static index.html with vanilla JS and plain CSS. No React, no build step, no bundler.

Features in scope:
- Conversation list in a left sidebar: create, rename, delete. Messages stored with role, content, model, token counts if the provider returns them, created_at.
- Streaming responses rendered token by token over Server-Sent Events. Stop button that aborts the upstream request mid-stream and saves the partial message.
- Provider adapters behind one interface: (1) any OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint, configured by base URL and key, (2) Ollama at http://localhost:11434. Model picker in the header, list pulled from the provider when it supports it, otherwise from a MODELS env var.
- Reusable system prompts: a small library table, assign one per conversation, edit inline.
- Markdown rendering with fenced code blocks, syntax highlighting optional, copy button on each block.
- Full text search across all messages using SQLite FTS5.
- Export a conversation as markdown to a file.

Explicitly out of scope: user accounts, auth, multi-tenancy, web search, tool calling, image input or output, voice, mobile apps, analytics, any hosted deployment story.

Secrets: read OPENAI_BASE_URL, OPENAI_API_KEY, MODELS from .env via Bun's built-in env loading. Ship a .env.example. Never commit .env, never log key values.

Deliverables: server.ts, public/index.html, public/app.js, public/style.css, schema in a migrations file run on boot, README with exactly the commands to install and run. It must work with `bun install && bun run server.ts` and nothing else.
